review.purpose: Use the shipped synthetic registry to choose the header profile for a focused repeated-identifier example.
review.finding: The registry exposes ADT and ORU samples. Their actual declared type/version accessors agree with the authored profile; ADT version 2.5 establishes this walkthrough scope while ORU observation interpretation is left outside it. The seven repetition fixtures are separate invented messages.

review.purpose: Distinguish message profiles and raw delimiter-dependent header text before applying a field interpretation.
review.finding: The shipped examples declare ADT^A01 and ORU^R01. The custom message C uses ADT*A01, so raw string equality with a caret-delimited type would miss the equivalent type/event shape. The field table supplies its actual separator.

review.purpose: Make the declared version assumption visible when choosing a sample profile.
review.finding: Both shipped examples declare version 2.5; the ADT type plus this declared version selects the illustrated profile. Missing version in the short header remains NULL and parser acceptance is not treated as conformance.

review.purpose: Separate message identity from the identifiers inside a repeating PID field.
review.finding: Four of seven invented rows carry control IDs, while five parse. The authored message_key preserves rows whose control ID is absent; a message control ID is not counted as a patient identifier or used to drop incomplete rows.

review.purpose: Keep rejected, missing, accepted-incomplete and usable inputs distinct in the counting population.
review.finding: The header-only message parses without inventing PID-3 or a control ID. An empty PID-3 is a known zero, whereas missing/rejected/NULL messages keep NULL counts and stay outside the count chart with explicit diagnostics.

review.purpose: Inspect source segment order and custom-delimiter text before expanding fields.
review.finding: Message C produces MSH then PID rows; the segment representation retains the raw custom-delimiter message and its order, while the field representation establishes the finer repetition grain.

review.purpose: Compare first-repetition access with full field expansion and expose the release limitation on MSH-2.
review.finding: The scalar PID-3 accessor equals repetition zero. For A it retains HOSP and omits later LAB/RESEARCH occurrences. The MSH-2 scalar truncates to a prefix, so complete encoding characters come from hl7_fields. Different locations are materialized separately to avoid the documented engine expression-merging issue.

review.purpose: Preserve identifier repetitions and declared component separators while evaluating a first-only selection policy.
review.finding: Expanded PID-3 rows retain message, segment and field repetition indices plus raw text. Selecting only repetition zero changes six occurrences to three and removes two namespaces; bare strings and namespace-qualified sample keys remain distinct measures, neither counting people.
